# `tests/fixtures/assets/3d-templates`

Every file the generator here produces is **original work by Astrum Forge Studios**, released under
the repository's Apache-2.0 licence. Nothing is derived from a third-party model, texture, or sound
pack, and nothing was downloaded.

| File                 | What it is                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `make-level-art.mjs` | The generator. It writes straight into `templates/3d-third-person/assets/` and `templates/3d-first-person/assets/`, because a template has to be self-contained: `create-ignifx` copies the directory verbatim. |

Run it with `node tests/fixtures/assets/3d-templates/make-level-art.mjs`.

## What it writes

| Output                                         | What it is                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `floor.png` (128×128)                          | A poured slab scored into bays, with a seeded speckle so a large `uvScale` still has something to resolve. |
| `wall.png` (128×128)                           | A ribbed panel with a skirting band, so a wall reads which way up it is.                                   |
| `crate.png` (128×128)                          | Planks, a diagonal brace, and a bevelled border. Tinted per template.                                      |
| `footstep.wav` / `blip.wav`                    | 22.05 kHz mono 16-bit PCM: low-passed noise, and two decaying sine partials.                               |
| `player.glb`, `companion.glb`, `viewmodel.glb` | Copies of `../3d/rig.glb` under the addresses each template needs.                                         |
| `hero.animator.json`                           | A copy of `../3d/hero.animator.json`.                                                                      |

## Where the pieces come from

- The PNG and WAV encoders are `../2d-templates/png.mjs` — a hand-written PNG chunk writer over
  `node:zlib` and a RIFF/WAVE header. No image or audio library is involved anywhere.
- The rig and its state machine are the Phase 7 fixtures in `../3d/`, generated by `make-rig.mjs`.
  They are **copied** rather than referenced: `create-ignifx` copies a template directory into a
  player's project, so a template cannot point at a path in this repository.
- Two of the copies are the same bytes under two names on purpose. `@ignifx/3d` binds one
  `Animator` per model asset — Babylon Lite binds an animation group to a single manager, and a
  cloned skinned mesh shares the template's skeleton — so the third-person player and its companion
  must load the rig under two different addresses to animate independently.

Every image and every sound is deterministic: the noise comes from a seeded generator, so a
regenerated file is byte for byte the file that is committed and a diff in review means a real
change.
